summary: Round 34 recheck, 05:14-05:40Z 29 Sep. I made 0 Kaggle calls and used no browser. At the 05:04:36Z poll, night probes 52-54 (exp89r, exp75, exp89p) are still PENDING. Following R32-PI/R33-PI, I restricted the lens to claims that decide today's finals card. V_pub has been exp87a (a CI file, 0.959) since 21:45Z, but every partner comparison on the card and in the rules was computed with V_pub = exp85a (non-CI). I re-ran the existing mc26 finals-pair model (scratchpad r26/mc26.py, unchanged) with VPUB=exp87a and R28-RC-C's revised CI prior (mean +0.0002, sd 0.001-0.0015). (A) exp89u (#37 + K) was rejected as a partner. That rejection came from the R26 note 'dominated by exp75 in all 15 mc26 runs' plus the default 'no exp89u'. With a CI V_pub the ranking flips: {exp87a, exp89u} is the model's best pair in 15 of 18 runs, bronze 0.813-0.875 against 0.751-0.851 for {exp87a, #37}. It loses only if K's private mean is <= ~+0.0003 (prior +0.0009). It is REVIVED CONDITIONALLY: build and dummy it now at no risk, ask the user when they are back (~06:00Z = 09:00 MSK), and submit it only in a morning slot that would otherwise be UNUSED. (B) The R25 rule (b) says that with a CI V_pub, exp75 is shown only as a trade at >= 0.955 and P3 {V_pub, #37} is shown first. That is UPHELD as a near-equal trade. P3 is ahead on bronze by 0.00-0.04 in 5 of 6 revised-prior runs, and P2 is ahead on silver in 6 of 6. But card v5 l.47 says the model 'was not recomputed' for another V_pub, and that is false: the exp87a rows exist in mc26_grid.txt from 28 Sep. The 12:03Z fill should print the exp87a numbers. (C) The JT pair {exp87a, exp85a} (best + closest neighbour) stays rejected. It is below P3 on bronze in 5 of 6 revised-prior runs (0.629-0.754 vs 0.708-0.783) and below exp89u in 6 of 6.

findings.what: exp89u = #37 (K2 cap 4) + K (ILP_DIVISION_WEIGHT 0.4 + READMIT_MIN_SCORE 0.94) as the finals partner. OLD VERDICT: rejected. round26/report.json l.43: 'exp89u is dominated by exp75 as a partner in all 15 mc26 runs, and its read would land after 21:37 MSK'. R26-A6 turned that into a user question. The user did not answer it, so the default became 'no exp89u' (CONTEXT 28 Sep 15:43Z). The card keeps a P4 row only 'if exp89u was submitted', captioned 'below P1 in all 15 runs'. EVIDENCE BEHIND IT: mc26_grid4 was run with VPUB = exp85a / exp89q / exp89s, all non-CI files. With a non-CI V_pub, exp75 (#37 + CI) is the partner that adds the lever V_pub lacks. WHAT CHANGED: (1) Since 21:45Z V_pub = exp87a (cap 6 + K + CI, 0.959). With a CI V_pub the three partners hedge different sets. #37 hedges {cap, K, CI}. exp75 hedges {cap, K} but not CI. exp89u hedges {cap, CI} and keeps K, which has the strongest private prior (N(+0.0009, 0.0012), P > 0 ~0.77). (2) R28-RC-C cut the CI private prior to a mean of +0.0002 with sd ~0.001. RE-RUN (same mc26.py; outputs scratchpad r34/mc34_vpub87a.txt, mc34_exp89u.txt, mc34_allpartners.txt). {exp87a, exp89u} is the best pair on bronze in 15 of 18 runs. Revised CI prior, base: 0.817-0.824 vs {exp87a, #37} 0.754-0.766 and {exp87a, exp75} 0.742-0.763. Seeds 23/37: 0.822/0.813 vs 0.766/0.756. overfit field: 0.875 vs 0.842. qpub0: 0.778 vs 0.701. Pessimistic insertion prior: 0.776 vs 0.711. CI mean 0: 0.813 vs 0.740. It also leads on silver and on E[value] (+0.2e-3). It ties at K_MU +0.0003 (0.717 vs 0.708-0.715). It loses at K_MU 0 (0.653 vs 0.695), at K_MU -0.0003 (0.604 vs 0.667), and at K_MU +0.0003 with RHO 0.5 (0.669 vs 0.700). The algebra behind it: with V = b + C + K + CI, the partner b + K pays whenever cap or CI fails on private while K holds. exp70g, exp79a and exp85a are never close (0.633-0.773). NEW VERDICT: REVIVED, CONDITIONAL. The earlier rejection used the wrong V_pub. Under the current V_pub it is the model's best partner unless K's private mean is <= ~+0.0003. The model is judgmental and only ranks (I-092). The old timing objection is also void: in the A-M1 slot (~08:45Z) a non-CI read lands ~15:45-16:25Z, before the 18:37Z card. In the A-M2 slot (by 11:30Z) it lands ~18:30-19:10Z, before the 20:00Z tick.

findings.what: The R25 rule (b), carried into EXP75 PARTNER RULE v2 (b) (CONTEXT 28 Sep 14:12Z) and card v5 steps 7-8: 'V_pub is a CI file: B {V_pub, exp75} only at >= 0.955, as a trade; P3 {V_pub, #37} first'. Its reason (R25-A4, 11:17Z) was '{V_pub, exp75} hedges only the cap lever. CI is hedged only by #37 or exp70g.' The card also carries model numbers from the exp85a era (P2 bronze ~0.75-0.93, P3 ~0.68-0.85) and the line 'the model was computed for exp85a; for another V_pub it was not recomputed' (l.47). WHAT CHANGED: V_pub = exp87a (CI) since 21:45Z, and R28-RC-C lowered the CI prior. The exp87a rows already existed (mc26_grid.txt l.105-219, 28 Sep). Under the old CI prior (+0.0005, sd 0.0008), P2 led P3 on bronze in 10 of 13 runs (base 0.821 vs 0.787), and P3 led only at CI_SD >= 0.0015. RE-RUN with the revised prior (+0.0002, sd 0.001-0.0015): P3 {exp87a, #37} bronze 0.751-0.783 vs P2 {exp87a, exp75} 0.705-0.797. P3 is ahead or level in 5 of 6. P2 is ahead only at CI_MU 0.0004 / sd 0.001. P2 is ahead on silver in 6 of 6 (+0.02-0.05). E[value] is level within 0.1e-3. NEW VERDICT: the rule is UPHELD as a near-equal trade, not a dominance. Its stated reason is half wrong: with a CI V_pub, exp75 still hedges cap and K, and the choice turns on the private CI sign only. The card's model numbers and its 'not recomputed' sentence are STALE and misleading for the 12:03Z fill. exp75's own read (window ~09:05-10:05Z) is a third public CI read on the same embryo. At >= 0.955 clean it moves CI_MU toward +0.0004, where P2 edges ahead. At 0.954 or below, P3 first stands.

findings.what: The 'best + closest neighbour' finals pair (John Taylor style; for us {exp87a 0.959, exp85a 0.958}, which differ only by CI). OLD VERDICT: not recommended (CONTEXT 28 Sep 16:32Z; card v5 l.30 and l.45). Reasons: overfitting risk (743929, Cyrus comment); the pair hedges one lever and leaves cap 6 and K unhedged; mc26 put {V_pub, exp70g} below P1 in every run. The user agreed ('согласен'). WHAT CHANGED: V_pub is now the CI file, so the neighbour pair is {exp87a, exp85a}, which hedges exactly the CI lever. That lever's prior was cut by R28-RC-C, so it looked worth re-testing. RE-RUN (VPUB=exp87a, revised CI prior): {exp87a, exp85a} bronze 0.629-0.754 vs P3 0.708-0.783 (below in 5 of 6 runs; the exception is CMODE=norm, 0.862 vs 0.851, i.e. a light-tailed cap prior). It is below {exp87a, exp89u} in 6 of 6 (by 0.04-0.10). It leads P3 on silver only when the CI sd is >= 0.0012-0.0015. The dummy-clip lab gives no independent support: exp85a - exp70g = +0.0013 all, 44b6 -0.0011, a 2-edge difference. NEW VERDICT: UPHELD. With a CI V_pub the neighbour pair insures only the lever with the smallest public step (+0.001) and leaves cap 6 and K, the two larger public steps, unhedged.
